# Docker

Container packaging for the [[stickfps]] game server. The only containerised service in the source
set.

## The image

Two-stage build on `node:22-slim`: a build stage that compiles TypeScript, then a runtime stage that
installs with `npm ci --omit=dev` and copies the compiled output. `EXPOSE 9090`.

Two-stage matters more than it looks for this service: the runtime image carries no TypeScript
compiler and no dev dependencies, which is most of the weight of a Node build. `npm ci` rather than
`npm install` pins to the lockfile, so the image is reproducible from the same commit.

## It was actually run

Unlike the deployment itself, the container was **built and executed locally** and verified through a
real `/healthz` request. That makes it one of the few pieces of [[stickfps]]'s infrastructure story
backed by an executed command rather than a written runbook — the wider limits are on
[[render-hosting]] and [[stickfps]].

## But it is not on the deployed path

The image belongs to the **Fly.io** route, which was the original target while the transport still
needed UDP. [[render-over-fly-io]] moved the documented deployment to a dashboard-configured build
(`npm install && npm run build`, `npm start`) that does not use this Dockerfile at all. `fly.toml`
survives in the tree with its UDP service removed.

So the repo carries a working container for a host it no longer targets. That is not obviously wrong
— it keeps the service portable to any container host and it is the only fully self-describing
deployment artefact present — but it should not be read as *how the thing is deployed*.

## A drift marker

The Dockerfile still declares a UDP port after UDP was removed:

`EXPOSE 10000/udp`

A leftover from geckos.io, retired in [[websocket-tcp-over-geckos-udp]]. Harmless — `EXPOSE` is
documentation, not a firewall rule — and precisely because it is harmless nothing forced it to be
updated. Catalogued with the rest in [[documentation-drift]].
